chapters.title: Reading the vision

chapters.title: Modern application
chapters.about: Holocaust, kibbutz galuyot, and the two stages of the prophecy

summary: Rabbi Beyda examines the prophecy of the dry bones in Yehezkel chapter 37, discussing its historical significance and its relevance to the modern State of Israel. He suggests that while the physical restoration of the Jewish people has been achieved, the next stage is to develop a society built on the values of the Torah and the mitzvot. The class explores the distinction between a state and a society, drawing on the ideas of Rabbi Sacks.
questions: How can an ancient prophecy remain relevant to the modern world?
What is the difference between the physical restoration of a state and the creation of a Jewish society?
Why does the prophecy of the dry bones involve two distinct stages?
How can we apply the values of the Torah to the modern State of Israel?
